statement: A pseudo-$\mathfrak U$-topos category is a locally $\mathfrak U$-small category with all $\mathfrak U$-small colimits and a small full strictly generating subcategory.
notes: The accessible condition is not part of this definition. Dense is the relevant modern formulation of strict generation here.

statement: Every pseudo-topos category has all small limits.

statement: The opposite of a pseudo-topos category need not be a pseudo-topos category; groups have no small cogenerating subcategory.

notes: Enough injectives alone is not asserted as a theorem for every category.

statement: A Grothendieck topos satisfies the cogenerator conclusion and its opposite is a pseudo-topos category.
A pseudo-topos morphism $f:X\to Y$ is represented contravariantly by a small-colimit-preserving functor $f^*:\mathcal F(Y)\to\mathcal F(X)$.
A pseudo-topos morphism is exact when its inverse image is left exact; for topoi this is the additional geometric-morphism condition.
The Yoneda functor $\mathcal M\to\operatorname{Cont}(\mathcal M^{op},\Ens)$ is an equivalence for a pseudo-topos category.
repair: Full faithfulness is Yoneda; essential surjectivity is the dual representability criterion.

statement: A functor out of a pseudo-topos category preserves all small colimits if and only if it is a left adjoint.
notes: The target must be locally small; no accessibility of the source is assumed.

statement: The right adjoint $f_*$ preserves all small limits and determines its left adjoint up to the unique isomorphism compatible with the adjunction.
repair: Standard adjunction and Yoneda argument; see p52 commentary.

repair: Keep the edition slip in the text; use SGA4 I.8.12.8 for the intended left-adjoint statement.

statement: A morphism may be specified by the adjoint pair $(f^*,f_*)$, its unit and its counit, satisfying the triangular identities.

The operation subsequently denoted $X\boxtimes Y$ was initially proposed as a bicategorical product of pseudo-topoi.
gap_or_error: The author retracts this interpretation in footnote3.
repair: The actual product has coefficient category M×N. For M=N=Set the tensor is Set and the actual product has coefficient category Set×Set, not an equivalent category. Full proof in p54 block.

statement: It remains to prove that $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi}C$ is closed under colimits in ordinary $\operatorname{Ind}C$.
gap_or_error: Besides the printed ambient-category slip, this is not a valid closure property in general.
repair: For C=countable sets and pi=aleph_0, Ind_{aleph_1}C≃Set. The ordinary-ind countable coproduct of singleton objects is the finite-image presheaf and fails countable continuity, so it is outside the restricted ind-category. Construct colimits intrinsically instead.
notes: The source literally prints “stable dans M_pi”; even correcting it to Ind(M_pi) does not rescue this route.

statement: $\operatorname{Ind}\prime(C)$ is the full subcategory of presheaves $F$ for which $C/F$ is filtered.
notes: The prime denotes the presheaf realization, rather than formal indexed systems.

statement: A map $\alpha:\operatorname{colim}_I h_{x_i}\to F$ is equivalently a compatible family $h_{x_i}\to F$.
repair: The colimit universal property.

statement: That compatible family is equivalently a functor $\varphi_\alpha:I\to C/F$ over $C$.
repair: Yoneda identifies the component map with an element of F(x_i); compatibility is exactly the category-of-elements condition.

statement: Proposition4.4.2: for filtered $I$, the map $\alpha$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\varphi_\alpha$ is final.
repair: The commentary spells out the elementwise factorization and eventual-equality proof; it does not need an a priori representability theorem.

statement: F1: every object of $C/F$ maps to some $\varphi_\alpha(i)$.
F2: every parallel pair into $\varphi_\alpha(i)$ is equalized by a later arrow of $I$.
For filtered $I$, F1 and F2 are equivalent to finality of $\varphi_\alpha$.
repair: They say every relevant comma category is nonempty and connected; two objects are first moved to a common index and then equalized.

statement: Finality of $\varphi_\alpha$ makes the map from the indexed representable colimit to $F$ invertible.
gap_or_error: The printed first colimit comparison in the proof has the wrong domains.
repair: The well-typed comparison is colim_I psi phi_alpha→colim_{C/F}psi=F.

statement: If $\alpha$ is invertible, F1 and F2 follow from filtered colimits of sets.
repair: Evaluate at c: every element is represented at a stage and equality of two elements holds at a later stage.

statement: Corollary4.4.3: $F\in\operatorname{Ind}\prime_\pi C$ if and only if $C/F$ receives a final functor from an ordered set grand devant $\pi$.
repair: Apply Proposition4.4.2 to the chosen ordered ind-presentation; conversely use the canonical category-of-elements presentation.
notes: The PDF really prints the unusual order “grande devant pi I”; no omitted I is supplied.

statement: A category is grand devant $\pi$ if it receives a final functor from a poset grand devant $\pi$.
notes: For small categories this is modern pi^+-filteredness, proved in the commentary.

statement: For an ordered category this agrees with the previous definition for ordered sets.
repair: Choose preimages above a ≤pi-sized family, then an upper bound in the source poset.

statement: A category grand devant $\pi$ is filtered.
repair: Final images of filtered categories are filtered.

statement: A final image of a category grand devant $\pi$ is again grand devant $\pi$.
repair: Compose the final functors.

statement: PF_pi1: every family of at most $\pi$ objects has a common target, including the empty family.
notes: The empty family requires nonemptiness.

statement: PF_pi2: every at-most-$\pi$ family of parallel arrows is simultaneously equalized after postcomposition.
Proposition4.4.4(a) and (b) are equivalent.
repair: For small J, the commentary proves the cocone criterion and constructs a final pi^+-directed poset explicitly, without using condition(c).
notes: The actual application J=C/F is small; no stronger universe-size assertion is inferred.

statement: Condition(c): every at-most-$\pi$ arrow set lies in a subcategory of that size with a terminal object.
Condition(d): the poset of bounded terminal subcategories is grand devant $\pi$, and its terminal-object functor is final.
notes: The finality clause was added later by the author; it cannot be discarded in general.

statement: Proposition4.4.4: condition(b) implies condition(c).
gap_or_error: The one-object category {1,p}, p²=p≠1, satisfies the filteredness conditions but has no terminal subcategory containing p.
repair: Keep the equivalence of(a),(b). Under rigidity (all endomorphisms identities), the bounded-terminal-subcategory criterion is valid, with a complete proof marked ours in the commentary.
notes: The counterexample is supplied by the edition’s footnote18.

statement: Condition(c) implies condition(d).
repair: Apply(c) to the union of ≤pi terminal subcategories for directedness, and to one such subcategory together with a parallel pair for finality.

statement: Condition(d) implies condition(a).
repair: With the added finality clause this is immediate from the definition.
notes: The old attempted F2 proof below is no longer required for the implication.

statement: The poset of terminal subcategories being directed does not by itself make its terminal-object functor final.
repair: For J=B{±1}, the terminal-subcategory poset is a singleton, while the comma category of its functor to J is discrete with two objects.
notes: Author’s footnote16.

statement: If every endomorphism of J is an identity, the extra finality clause is unnecessary.
repair: The commentary proves this and the strengthened bounded-subcategory formulation explicitly: adjoining a cocone cannot create distinct arrows into the proposed terminal object under rigidity.

statement: The one-object idempotent category satisfies(a),(b), but neither(c) nor(d).
repair: Postcomposition with p equalizes every family. A subcategory containing p has two endomorphisms at its only object; the only terminal subcategory is identity-only, and its inclusion is not final.
notes: Editorial footnote18, independently verified by the commentary.

statement: Alternative(e): for every $|A|\leq\pi$, the diagonal $J\to J^A$ is final.
repair: For small J and infinite pi this is equivalent to pi^+-filteredness. The empty A enforces nonempty connected J, and finality expresses commutation of J-colimits with these products.

statement: Alternative(e\prime): finality of one diagonal $J\to J^{A_0}$ with $|A_0|=\pi$ is sufficient without further hypotheses.
gap_or_error: The empty category satisfies this when A_0 is nonempty, but is not filtered.
repair: Add J nonempty. Finality gives connectedness, and padding smaller product families with singleton diagrams reduces(e) to(e′).

statement: The attempted F2 argument using three terminal subcategories proves finality without the added hypothesis.
gap_or_error: The case where the source and selected terminal object coincide is precisely an endomorphism obstruction, acknowledged in footnote20.
repair: Under(c) include the two arrows themselves before forming a terminal enlargement; under(d) use its explicit finality clause.

statement: Corollary4.4.5: $F\in\operatorname{Ind}\prime_\pi C$ if and only if $C/F$ satisfies all four conditions of4.4.4.
gap_or_error: Conditions(c),(d) are too strong because of idempotents.
repair: Require condition(a) or(b), equivalently that C/F is pi^+-filtered. The category-of-elements and final-poset proofs are given in the commentary.

statement: Corollary4.4.6: a category with all colimits of at most $\pi$ arrows is grand devant $\pi$.
repair: It has cocones for every such diagram, hence PF_pi1 and PF_pi2. In the small case, use the corrected(a)⇔(b) proof, not the false(b)⇒(c).

statement: The inclusion $\alpha:C\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Ind}\prime_\pi C$ is fully faithful and preserves existing colimits of at most $\pi$ arrows.
repair: Full faithfulness is Yoneda; colimit preservation was proved on p.78.

statement: The induced functor on J-diagrams is fully faithful and preserves those colimits.
repair: Natural transformations are componentwise and diagram-category colimits are pointwise.

statement: For $j\in J$, $\varepsilon_j:e\to J$ selects j and induces evaluation functors.
notes: The displayed e_j(e) is an edition slip for epsilon_j(e). The heading4.4.6 duplicates the preceding corollary number; automatic renumbering to4.4.7 would collide with the later lemma.

statement: The evaluation square induces $\varepsilon_j^\varphi:I=\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)/\varphi\to C/\varphi(j)$.
notes: The source prints Hom(J/C), an edition slip for Hom(J,C).

statement: If C has a specified class of colimits of size at most pi, so do Fun(J,C), its comma category over phi, and C/phi(j).
repair: Take underlying colimits, use preservation by alpha and alpha^J, and form the induced structure map to phi.

statement: The induced evaluation functor between comma categories preserves these colimits.
repair: Pointwise evaluation preserves the colimit construction and its structure map.

statement: If C is finitely cocomplete, both comma categories are filtered.
repair: Finite colimits supply all finite cocones, including nonemptiness.

statement: If all evaluation functors $\varepsilon_j^\varphi$ are final, phi is the pointwise colimit of its canonical coherent approximations.
repair: At each vertex use finality and the canonical presentation of phi(j) by C/phi(j).

statement: The index $I=\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)/\varphi$ is an ordered filtered set.
gap_or_error: It is generally a category with parallel maps, not a poset.
repair: Read “filtered category”; if an ordered presentation is needed, apply the final-directed-poset replacement.

statement: $\varphi(j)=\varepsilon_j^*(\varphi)$ and the displayed composite evaluates its coherent approximations.

statement: Currying the canonical approximation functor gives $\psi:I\times J\to C$ with $\varphi(j)\cong\operatorname{colim}_I\psi(i,j)$.
gap_or_error: The PDF first uses uppercase Psi for this functor, then lowercase psi.
repair: Use lowercase psi consistently in the explanation, preserving the source notation in the transcription.

statement: When J-colimits exist in C and $|\operatorname{Fl}J|\leq\pi$, the two candidate iterated colimits have the same universal property.

notes: A magnified PDF crop confirms that the preceding sentence correctly says type J; no transcription correction is needed.

repair: The representation is coherent because I consists of whole diagrams with natural transformations to phi.

statement: Define $\Psi(i)=\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\psi(i,j)$ in C; the same colimit is valid in the restricted ind-category.

statement: Corollary4.4.8: if C is ≤pi-cocomplete, so are Fun(J,C) and I; thus I is grand devant pi.

statement: Lemma4.4.8.1: a pi^+-filtered colimit of objects of C exists in the restricted ind-category and is the presheaf colimit.
repair: Choose a final pi^+-directed poset and use the definition of the restricted ind-category.

statement: The preceding lemma is equivalent to closure of the restricted ind-category under all pi^+-filtered colimits of its objects.

statement: To establish ≤pi-small colimits intrinsically it now suffices to prove finality of the evaluation comma functors.
repair: Combine Lemma4.4.7, Corollary4.4.8, and Lemma4.4.8.1.

statement: Lemma4.4.9: each evaluation comma functor has a left adjoint if $|J(j,j\prime)|\leq\pi$.

statement: A functor having a left adjoint is final.
repair: Each comma category from an object to the functor has the universal arrow as an initial object, hence is nonempty and connected.

statement: Evaluation on C-valued J-diagrams has the left adjoint $(L_jc)(j\prime)=\coprod_{J(j,j\prime)}c$.
repair: A natural transformation out of this copower diagram is uniquely determined by the identity summand at j; the commentary gives the complete formula.

statement: The analogous evaluation on restricted-ind-valued diagrams has a left adjoint because the required coproducts exist there.
gap_or_error: Existence of those coproducts for arbitrary ind-objects is temporarily assumed and is reserved in the continuation on p.91.
repair: For the comma adjunction actually needed, only coproducts of representable objects are used; these already exist by the proof on p.78.

statement: The base-change map $\lambda\prime\gamma\to\beta\lambda$ is an isomorphism.
gap_or_error: The notation presupposes the two ambient evaluation adjoints; one is at this stage provisional.
repair: On each representable c, the map identifies the corresponding Hom_J(j,j′)-copowers, which alpha preserves. This restricted calculation suffices for the comma adjoint.

statement: The comma-level left adjoint is obtained from the evaluation adjunctions and the invertible base-change map.
repair: The general mates argument is developed in Lemma4.4.10 on pp.91–93; the commentary gives the specialized explicit construction here.
notes: The source heading says proof4.4.8, but the statement being proved is4.4.9.

statement: In (4.4.9.1), the mate $\lambda^{\prime}\gamma\to\beta\lambda$ is invertible when the inclusion $C\to\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}(C)$ preserves the copowers indexed by $J(j,j\prime)$.
gap_or_error: The source defers existence of the needed coproducts to Lemma 4.4.11; the printed reference (4.4.4.2) is a cross-reference slip.
repair: Use preservation of these particular copowers, established by the bounded-colimit argument; the target comparison is (4.4.9.2).
notes: Continuation of Lemma 4.4.9 from pp89–90; a direct comma-adjunction proof avoids presupposing arbitrary coproducts in the completion.

statement: Lemma 4.4.10: if $\varepsilon$ has left adjoint $\lambda$, $\varepsilon^{\prime}$ has left adjoint $\lambda^{\prime}$, and the canonical mate is invertible, then $(\beta\downarrow y\prime)\to(\gamma\downarrow\varepsilon^{\prime} y\prime)$ has a left adjoint.
gap_or_error: Grothendieck expressly says that he has not carried the verification to its last detail.
repair: The p92 commentary proves a natural bijection of comma-category Hom sets by transposing the equation defining an arrow; this supplies a complete proof.
notes: The source writes B/y0\prime and C/z0\prime for these comma categories, not ordinary slices of B and C at objects in them.

statement: The left adjoint of Lemma 4.4.10 sends $(c,v:\gamma c\to\varepsilon^{\prime} y\prime)$ to $(\lambda c,\epsilon^{\prime}_{y\prime}\lambda^{\prime}(v)\chi_c^{-1})$, where $\chi:\lambda^{\prime}\gamma\simeq\beta\lambda$.
repair: Functoriality and the adjunction are checked in the same p92 block.

statement: Lemma 4.4.11: if $C$ has coproducts with at most $\pi$ summands, then $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C$ has those coproducts.
repair: Take the product of the categories of elements, form the coproduct at each representable stage, then take its $\pi^+$-filtered colimit; the Hom calculation is written out in the p94 block.
notes: The proof is completed through Lemma 4.4.12; only the coproduct hypothesis on C is needed.

statement: Under Lemma 4.4.11, the canonical embedding $C\to\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C$ preserves coproducts with at most $\pi$ summands.
notes: The source recalls the preservation assertion already established for bounded colimits.

statement: For discrete $J$, the category $C^J/\varphi$ is canonically $\prod_{j\in J}(C/\varphi_j)$ and its evaluation functor is the corresponding projection.
notes: Includes the empty product, which is terminal.

statement: Lemma 4.4.12: any small product of $\pi^+$-filtered small categories is $\pi^+$-filtered.
repair: Choose a cocone independently in each coordinate for a common diagram with at most pi arrows; the product of these cocones is a cocone.
notes: Uses the axiom of choice for the small family of coordinates; no bound on the number of factors beyond smallness is required.

statement: Every projection from a small product of $\pi^+$-filtered categories to one factor is final.
repair: Its comma category is the product of one undercategory with the remaining factors; this is nonempty and filtered, hence connected.
notes: The empty family has no projection; the claim is for a chosen factor.

statement: An infinite product of nonempty connected categories need not be connected.
repair: The p94 commentary gives connected finite height-two zigzag posets with unbounded endpoint distance; the two endpoint tuples in their product cannot be joined by a finite zigzag.

statement: Any small product of ordinary filtered categories is filtered.
repair: The coordinatewise cocone proof of Lemma 4.4.12 applies to finite diagrams.

statement: Question/negative expectation: even if $C$ has colimits of cardinal at most $\pi$, evaluation $C^J/\varphi\to C/\varphi(j)$ need not be final for $\varphi:J\to\operatorname{Ind}(C)$.
repair: Proved negative in the p94 example: C is a skeleton of countable sets, J=BZ, and F(c) is the set of finite-image maps c→Z with translation action. Every equivariant representable presentation has empty domain; the comma category above 1→F choosing 0 is empty.
references: Henry2025 (broader comparison theorem; the explicit finite-image calculation is supplied here).
notes: The counterexample retains C countably cocomplete and J countable; ordinary filteredness is the lost hypothesis.

statement: The embedding $C\to\operatorname{Ind}(C)$ preserves finite colimits that exist in $C$, but need not preserve coproducts of size at most an infinite $\pi$.
repair: For countable sets C, the ordinary-Ind coproduct of countably many representable singletons is the filtered presheaf colimit of their finite coproducts in Ind(C). Evaluated at c, it consists of the finite-image maps c→N and therefore differs from the representable h_N.
notes: This explains why the copower adjunction proof does not directly apply to ordinary Ind.

statement: For $C$ closed under colimits of cardinal at most $\pi$, a diagram of that size in $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}(C)$ admits a simultaneous presentation $I\times J\to C$ with $I$ $\pi^+$-filtered.
notes: Summary of Lemmas4.4.7–4.4.12; the size condition is on arrows of J.

statement: The index $I$ in such a presentation may be replaced by a $\pi^+$-directed poset through a final functor.
repair: Apply the standard directed-poset replacement for a small filtered category at the same regular cardinal.
notes: This does not use the invalid terminal-subcategory characterization in4.4.4(c,d).

statement: Theorem4.4.13(a): $C\to\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C$ preserves colimits indexed by categories with at most $\pi$ arrows.
notes: Repeated for reference from the preceding argument.

statement: Theorem4.4.13(b): every diagram $\varphi:J\to\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C$ with $|\operatorname{Fl}J|\leq\pi$ has a simultaneous presentation by $I\times J\to C$ with I a $\pi^+$-directed poset.
For this presentation, $\varinjlim_J\varphi\simeq\varinjlim_{i\in I}y(\varinjlim_{j\in J}c_{ij})$, where the inner colimit is taken in C and the outer colimit is a $\pi^+$-filtered presheaf colimit.
notes: Existence follows from the bounded colimits of C and closure under the filtered colimit of representables; the universal property is checked by mapping into arbitrary Ind objects.

statement: Theorem4.4.13(c): if C is essentially small and has all colimits of size at most pi, then $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C$ is cocomplete.
repair: Completed on pp97–100 using4.4.14 and4.4.15.
notes: Correct statement; the later failure of a fixed cardinal filtration does not undermine this unbounded cocompleteness result.

statement: $\mathcal I_\pi(J)$ is the poset of subcategories K of J with at most pi arrows, ordered by inclusion.
notes: The empty subcategory is included.

statement: For every small J and infinite pi, $\mathcal I_\pi(J)$ is $\pi^+$-directed.
notes: Take the subcategory generated by the union of at most pi arrow sets; finite composition closure still has size at most pi.

statement: Corollary4.4.14: a category with colimits of size at most pi and colimits indexed by all small $\pi^+$-directed posets has all small colimits.
repair: The p98 commentary proves the cocone equivalence for the decomposition by small subcategories.
notes: No small generating set or accessibility assumption is required.

statement: For X:J→M, $\varinjlim_JX\simeq\varinjlim_{K\in\mathcal I_\pi(J)}\varinjlim_KX$ whenever the inner colimits exist and either side of the outer universal property is represented.
notes: The same cocones are represented; this is not an interchange presupposing both colimits.

statement: Corollary4.4.14.1: a functor preserving the two classes of colimits in4.4.14 preserves every small colimit.
repair: Apply the same cocone decomposition to the functor and its canonical comparison maps.
notes: Stated in footnote27.

statement: Corollary4.4.15: for any small C, $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C$ is closed in $\widehat C$ under small $\pi^+$-filtered colimits, and the inclusion preserves/creates these colimits.
notes: No bounded-colimit assumption on C; this is stronger than being a filtered colimit of representables by definition.

statement: For a $\pi^+$-filtered colimit F of such presheaves, any at-most-pi family of objects of C/F has a common receiving object.
notes: Lift all defining elements to one stage; then use filteredness of that stage’s category of elements.

statement: For the same F, any at-most-pi family of parallel arrows in C/F can be made equal after composition with one arrow.

statement: Corollary4.4.16: restriction induces $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C,E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\leq\pi\text{-colim}}(C,E)$ for every cocomplete locally small E.

statement: The embedding $\alpha:C\to\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}C$ is fully faithful, its image is dense, and it preserves colimits of size at most pi.

statement: Claim as written: unrestricted restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(M,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,E)$ is fully faithful because C strictly generates M.

statement: Proposition4.5.2 as first stated: conditions a,a\prime,a\prime\prime,b,c,c\prime are equivalent for every pi≥pi1.

statement: Footnote53 retains strict epimorphy for the special axes H→H×H with H nontrivial.
gap_or_error: Compatibility on their trivial intersection does not impose commutation of images.
repair: Maps from both copies of H to H*H form a compatible pair with no extension to H×H. Replace H×H by C2*C2 for the desired nonuniversal-family example.
notes: PDF leaf44 confirms the erroneous special-case claim.

statement: Pulling the two axes H→H×H back along the diagonal H→H×H gives two copies of1→H, which are not a strict epimorphic family for H≠1.
repair: The pullback calculation is correct. It cannot show failure of universality of strict families because the original axes were not strict.

statement: Corollary4.5.15: under C and pi>=pi1, D_pi is exactly the class of objects with a universal strict epimorphic family of<=pi maps from C.
repair: Use a filtered-poset C-presentation of size<=pi; C makes its cocone universally strict. The converse is the strict-family presentation argument at130–131.
notes: Use the corrected colimit interpretation of Filt-prime, not the inequivalent cofinality interpretation.

statement: Under C, the cocone of every ordinary filtered colimit is a universal strict epimorphic family.
repair: After any base change it is still a colimit cocone; every colimit cocone is strictly epimorphic.

statement: Corollary4.5.16: under C, an object covered by a universally epimorphic family of<=pi objects in D_pi belongs to D_pi.
gap_or_error: The outer family is only universally epimorphic; it need not supply the relations required for a bounded presentation.
repair: In the locally aleph1-presentable category of sets with one countably-ary relation, all colimits are universal. For pi=beth_omega and |S|=pi, (S,empty)→(S,S^N) is universally epimorphic; its source is a pi-small coproduct of C objects, but its target is not pi^+-presentable. Full proof in commentary atp137. Strengthen the outer family to universally strict epimorphic to repair.
notes: Every ambient hypothesis is verified. This is a counterexample to the complete stated proposition, not merely its proof step.

statement: A universally epimorphic outer family composed with universal strict epimorphic inner families is universally strict epimorphic.
gap_or_error: Strictness cannot be inferred by this transitivity argument.
repair: In Pos, discrete2→chain2 is universally epimorphic but not strict; take identity inner cover. Add strictness to the outer family.
notes: The Pos example isolates this inference; the separate countably-ary relation example refutes Cor4.5.16 under all its hypotheses.

statement: The union of<=pi inner covers each with<=pi terms has<=pi terms.
repair: pi*pi=pi for infinite pi.

statement: Proposition4.5.17: M_pi is the smallest strictly full subcategory containing C and closed under colimits with at most pi arrows, for pi>=pi0.
repair: Closure gives one inclusion. A pi^+-filtered presentation gives a retract for the other; coequalizer closure includes all retracts. This uses only the valid a⇒c portion of the corrected lemma.

statement: Closing C only under pi0^+-filtered colimits of arrow-cardinality<=pi gives Filt^pi and may give a proper subcategory of M_pi.
repair: For pi>=pi1, the bounded presheaf-value characterization and its filtered canonical presentation prove this. Set with pi^(pi0)>pi shows strict inclusion.
notes: The stated definition of Filt^pi begins at pi1; do not silently extend the equality to pi<pi1.

statement: The one-step class of arbitrary colimits of<=pi-arrow diagrams in C need not equal M_pi.
gap_or_error: This warning confuses iterated closure with a one-step class that is in fact already closed under the required colimits.
repair: The explicit coequalizer-flattening theorem in the p128 commentary proves equality for every pi>=pi0. The general result is known, and Barton gives a primary proof.
notes: This correction does not remove the distinct arithmetic obstruction for pi0^+-filtered presentations.
